items.title: IDC Frontier (IDCF Cloud), Japan — 495 customers down
items.summary: The SoftBank subsidiary confirmed a ransomware attack that began Oct 7 at 3:40 AM local time and forced a network and system shutdown, taking 495 companies and local governments offline; the attacker, data theft and full restoration time remain unconfirmed.

items.title: Advantest confirms data theft, 233 days after intrusion
items.summary: The Japanese chip-test equipment maker confirmed on Oct 7 that personal data was stolen in a ransomware attack first detected earlier this year, a 233-day gap between discovery and breach notice.

items.title: Osaka Metropolitan University — ~500 servers offline
items.summary: Around 500 servers went offline, the campus network was unavailable and classes were cancelled; data on at least 130,000 students and staff may have been exposed (aggregator report).

items.title: City of Vicksburg, Mississippi
items.summary: City computer systems were temporarily shut down after an attack, while police, fire and 911 services stayed operational (aggregator report).

items.title: Svedala municipality, Sweden
items.summary: All municipal IT systems went down after a ransomware attack, and the municipality is investigating how far the attackers penetrated (aggregator report).

items.title: Warlock ransomware via compromised SharePoint servers
items.summary: Check Point documented Warlock ransomware deployed across at least 33 hosts in a single intrusion that used compromised SharePoint servers for initial access.

items.title: Qilin lists Japanese electronics manufacturer
items.summary: CYFIRMA observed a Japanese electronics manufacturer posted on Qilin's dark web leak site; the claim is not confirmed by the victim.

ransomware.note: Osaka, Vicksburg and Svedala come from an aggregator and could not be dated precisely or checked against primary reporting this run.

items.title: IDCF Cloud region outage (ransomware-driven)
items.summary: IDC Frontier's cloud platform has been disrupted since Oct 7, with 495 corporate and local-government tenants affected and no confirmed time for full restoration as of Oct 9.

items.title: Azure — two incidents across 18 regions in 40 hours
items.summary: Between Sep 29 and Oct 1, two separate Azure outages knocked gateway services offline across 18 regions and left Azure OpenAI customers in Sweden with failed API calls for nearly six hours.

items.title: Microsoft 365 — Exchange hybrid mail delivery issue
items.summary: A minor incident logged Oct 8: some messages from on-premises Exchange servers to Exchange Online may intermittently fail, with very few user reports.

items.title: Cloudflare — Keyless SSL TLS handshake failures
items.summary: On Oct 6 from 08:22 to 09:06 UTC, TLS handshakes failed for some Keyless SSL customers using RSA keys with specific key-backend configurations; three smaller Oct 5 incidents were also resolved.

outage.note: No major AWS or Google Cloud incident found for October so far; items are from status aggregators, not provider post-incident reports.

items.title: CISA adds Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88779 to KEV
items.summary: On Oct 4 CISA added a NetScaler memory buffer flaw to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on evidence of active exploitation.

items.title: CISA adds two Zammad flaws to KEV
items.summary: On Oct 2 CISA added CVE-2026-102489 (session fixation, rated 9.8 by one tracker) and CVE-2026-102490 (improper privilege management) in the Zammad helpdesk software.

items.title: DIVD breached via Zammad zero-days by an autonomous AI agent
items.summary: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure said it was hacked in an attack carried out by an autonomous AI agent that found two previously unknown Zammad zero-days; these appear to be the flaws CISA added Oct 2, though no source states the match explicitly.

items.title: Pentagon DMDC file-transfer system — months-long breach
items.summary: A file transfer system used by the Defense Manpower Data Center, the Pentagon's records-keeping unit, was compromised in a breach running from October 2025 to July 2026.

items.title: Double Counter (Discord bot) — 28 million accounts
items.summary: A breach at Discord verification service Double Counter exposed IDs, IP data and emails for 28 million accounts; the company says no passwords or stored card numbers were exposed, but $7,316 was fraudulently charged.

items.title: Fortinet FortiMail CVE-2026-104286 reported as Oct 1 KEV add
items.summary: A third-party tracker identifies CISA's Oct 1 single-entry KEV addition as a FortiMail path traversal flaw; not confirmed against CISA's own alert, and the tracker notes a due-date discrepancy.

items.title: KEV pace: 247 additions in 2026, already past all of 2025
items.summary: A secondary analysis counts 247 KEV entries added Jan 1 to Oct 1, 2026 versus 245 in all of 2025, with 91 of 114 entries since BOD 26-04 carrying a three-day remediation deadline.

items.title: Hurricane Isaias — Gulf Coast landfall forecast late Oct 9
items.summary: Category 2 Isaias was forecast to briefly reach major-hurricane strength before landfall late Friday; Florida, Alabama and Georgia declared states of emergency, with mandatory evacuations in coastal Okaloosa County and Dauphin Island's west end, airport closures, and Chevron and Shell shutting in some offshore production.

items.title: Bouquet Fire, Santa Clarita, California
items.summary: Cal Fire ordered evacuations on Oct 3 for a fire northeast of Santa Clarita that had reached 843 acres at 0% containment; no later update was found this run.

items.title: Earthquake — 102 km NE of Norsup, Vanuatu (Oct 08)
items.summary: Magnitude 6.3; USGS PAGER alert green, no tsunami flag.

items.title: Earthquake — 92 km NNW of Aleneva, Alaska (Oct 06)
items.summary: Magnitude 5.5; USGS PAGER alert green, no tsunami flag.

items.title: Earthquake — 5 km NNE of Korumburra, Australia (Oct 02)
items.summary: Magnitude 4.7; USGS PAGER alert green, no tsunami flag.

physical.note: Isaias details are as of Oct 8 reporting; check the National Hurricane Center for the current track and intensity.
